subject: business-studies
title: Gearing and Limitations
welcome_lead: Gearing measures debt risk - and ratios always need context.
meta_desc: A-Level Ratio Analysis: gearing ratio and limitations of ratios.
final_note: High gearing magnifies returns and risk; ratios are a starting point, not a verdict.

concepts.def: Long-term debt as a share of total long-term capital.
Operating profit divided by interest payable.
Manipulating accounts at year-end to flatter ratios.

walkthroughs.body_html: Gearing = long-term liabilities / (capital + long-term liabilities) x 100. Utilities and infrastructure firms run at 60 to 80 percent; tech firms often under 10 percent.
High gearing means high interest bills. If profits fall, interest still has to be paid - high-geared firms are first to fail in a recession but can amplify returns in booms.
Ratios use historic data. Inflation, accounting policies and seasonality distort comparisons. Always combine ratios with qualitative analysis and benchmark over several years.
